newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut towns to get more police officers.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut towns to get more police officers.

text.p: Connecticut towns will receive more police officers to the tune of $3.41 million, the state's U.S. Senators Chris Dodd and Joe Lieberman said in a joint statement on Wednesday.
The funds from the U.S. Department of Justice are to hire a total of 45 additional full-time and three part-time police officers.
The city of Bridgeport will receive the biggest chunk -- some $1.35 million for 18 full-time officers.

Other towns, cities and institutions to receive funding are: Ansonia, Berlin, Central Connecticut State Universitsy, Derby, East Windsor, Eastern Connecticut State University, Essex, Manchester, New Fairfield, Oxford, Prospect, South Windsor, Stratford, Suffield and Willimantic.
"This funding will give police departments the physical manpower necessary to combat violence and seriously reduce drug use in our state," said Dodd.
